1321.quote_or_event: “Everyone makes mistakes; only the Guru and the Creator are infallible.”
1321.explanation: Guru Nanak teaches that every person errs, but the Guru and the Creator are without fault.
1321.tie_back: The Kural's wife admits there is no fault in her beloved and sulks anyway; Gurbani's soul-bride likewise knows the faults are all on her side and that the Beloved is faultless.
1321.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 61, Siree Raag, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1321._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via the BaniDB API (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; partial: both affirm the Beloved has no fault, but Gurbani has no playful sulking, and its love is spiritual, for God, not romantic.

1322.quote_or_event: “Suffering is the medicine, and pleasure the disease, because where there is pleasure, there is no desire for God.”
1322.explanation: Guru Nanak teaches that pain can heal the soul by renewing its longing for God, while easy comfort makes it forget.
1322.tie_back: The Kural says the small pain of a sulk makes love wilt only to bloom more richly; Gurbani likewise sees passing pain as the medicine that makes longing for the Beloved grow.
1322.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 469, Raag Aasaa (Asa di Vaar), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1322._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via the BaniDB API (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; reasonable but partial: both see a little pain as deepening love, though Gurbani speaks of spiritual longing for God, not romantic love.

1323.quote_or_event: “I do not seek power, and I do not seek liberation. My mind is in love with Your Lotus Feet.”
1323.explanation: Guru Arjan says he wants neither worldly power nor even liberation, only loving closeness to the Lord.
1323.tie_back: The Kural asks whether any heaven could match the sweetness of loving one whose heart is blended with one's own; Gurbani likewise prizes love for the Beloved above every heaven or reward.
1323.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 534, Raag Dayv Gandhaaree, Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1323._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via the BaniDB API (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; strong thematic fit on love outranking heaven, but the love here is spiritual love for God, not romantic love, and there is no sulking.

1324.quote_or_event: “The Bani of the Lord's Love is the pointed arrow, which has pierced my mind, O Lord King.”
1324.explanation: Guru Ram Das describes the Lord's loving Word as an arrow that pierces the heart and overcomes it.
1324.tie_back: The Kural speaks of a weapon hidden in the lover's embrace that breaks down the wife's resolve to keep sulking; Gurbani likewise pictures love as a weapon that pierces and conquers the mind.
1324.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 449, Raag Aasaa (Chhant), Guru Ram Das (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1324._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via the BaniDB API (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; strong image match (love as a weapon that overcomes the heart), but this is spiritual love for God, not romantic love.

1325.quote_or_event: “Many talk of the pain and suffering of separation; O pain, you are the ruler of all.”
1325.explanation: Sheikh Farid, whose verses the Gurus included in the Guru Granth Sahib, calls the pain of separation from the Beloved the sovereign of all feelings, because it keeps love alive.
1325.tie_back: The Kural says that being kept apart from the beloved, even without fault, holds a pleasure of its own; Farid likewise honours the ache of separation as a royal and precious part of love.
1325.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1379, Salok Sheikh Fareed (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1325._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via the BaniDB API (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; partial: both value the state of being apart, but Farid stresses its pain rather than its pleasure, and the love is spiritual, not romantic.

1326.quote_or_event: “Your actions seem so sweet to me.”
1326.explanation: Guru Arjan accepts whatever the Lord does, near or distant, as sweet, because it comes from the Beloved.
1326.tie_back: The Kural finds the sulk sweeter than union itself, as digesting is sweeter than eating; Gurbani similarly finds sweetness even in the Beloved's withholding, though it makes no such ranking.
1326.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 394, Raag Aasaa, Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1326._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via the BaniDB API (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: Gurbani has no parallel to the Kural's claim that the quarrel beats the union or to its digestion image; this is spiritual, not romantic, love.

1327.quote_or_event: “When something is placed on the balancing scale and weighed, the side which descends is heavier.”
1327.explanation: Guru Nanak teaches that the one who bows low in humility is the one who truly carries weight and wins honour.
1327.tie_back: The Kural says that in a lovers' quarrel the one who gives in first is the real winner; Gurbani likewise teaches that the one who bows down comes out the heavier and greater.
1327.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 470, Raag Aasaa (Asa di Vaar), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1327._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via the BaniDB API (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; strong fit on the paradox that yielding is winning, though Gurbani teaches humility in general, not within a romantic quarrel.

1328.quote_or_event: “God unites the separated souls with Himself, awakening their destiny.”
1328.explanation: Guru Nanak teaches that God Himself brings back together those who have been separated from Him.
1328.tie_back: The Kural's husband hopes a little sulking will once more win back the sweetness of reunion; Gurbani likewise trusts that the separated are brought back into union with the Beloved.
1328.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 934, Raag Raamkalee (Dakhni Oankaar), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1328._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via the BaniDB API (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; partial: both look to reunion after separation, but in Gurbani the reunion is God's grace, not won by sulking, and the love is spiritual, not romantic.

1329.quote_or_event: “Fareed, musk is released at night. Those who are sleeping do not receive their share.”
1329.explanation: Sheikh Farid, whose verses are in the Guru Granth Sahib, teaches that the night hours are precious for the lover of God, who stays awake to seek the Beloved.
1329.tie_back: The Kural's lover wishes the night would stretch on so he can keep pleading with his beloved; Farid likewise treasures the night as the time for longing and entreaty.
1329.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1382, Salok Sheikh Fareed (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1329._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via the BaniDB API (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: both prize the night for seeking the beloved, but Farid speaks of prayerful wakefulness for God, not a lover's pleading.

1330.quote_or_event: “Auspicious is that day, when God, the lofty, inaccessible and infinite, hugs me close in His embrace.”
1330.explanation: Guru Arjan, in the voice of the soul-bride, rejoices in the day the infinite Lord takes her into His embrace.
1330.tie_back: The Kural's last couplet says the crowning delight of love is to be held close again after the sulk; Gurbani likewise crowns the soul's longing with the Beloved's embrace.
1330.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 546, Raag Bihaagraa (Chhant), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1330._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via the BaniDB API (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; strong fit on union crowned by embrace, but this is the bride-soul's spiritual union with God, not romantic love, and there is no sulking.
